title: Arc 2/5: rename Story to Arc, keeping Story as a resolving alias
summary: The flip itself, atomic with the e2e harness because that gate asserts story.schema.json.
description: Rename the profile type (profile.ts:965), the builtin-template key (template.ts:501) and TYPE_DIRECTORIES (schema.ts:333, Arc -> arcs), retaining Story as a deprecated alias from Arc 1/5. Regenerate .lore/schemas so arc.schema.json replaces story.schema.json. MUST be atomic with docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh: that harness asserts .lore/schemas/story.schema.json parses in three loops (1373, 1413, 1583) plus an rm -f at 1418, and it is a REQUIRED context on dev, so a split would land a red gate. Alias is RESOLVE-ONLY: no story.schema.json is emitted.

acceptanceCriteria.text: profile.ts declares Arc; Story resolves to it as a deprecated alias
TYPE_DIRECTORIES maps Arc to arcs, and the builtin template resolves for Arc
lore schema export emits arc.schema.json and prunes story.schema.json, and a no-op re-run is byte-identical
docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh updated in the SAME commit; the docker e2e harness context is green on the PR head
An existing type: Story document still validates (warning only) and still accepts lore link -- the regression this whole migration exists to prevent
npm run check and lore check both exit 0

implementationNotes:
SCOPE UPDATED FROM MEASUREMENT, two changes — one removes work, one adds it.

1. ATOMICITY WITH THE E2E HARNESS IS NO LONGER REQUIRED. Proven rather than inferred, which is what opum-agent asked for. Under ruling (c) the alias owns its slug, so `lore schema export` against an Arc+Story-alias profile emits BOTH arc.schema.json and story.schema.json. Measured against the local build in a scratch bundle: the harness's verbatim assertion form `jq -e . .lore/schemas/<T>.schema.json` passes 6 of 6, and `lore check` reports 0 errors, so the retained file is OWNED rather than orphaned. The three slug loops (run-e2e.sh 1373, 1413, 1583) and the rm -f at 1418 therefore pass UNCHANGED.

SCOPE OF THAT PROOF, kept narrow on purpose and agreed with opum-agent: I measured the specific assertions previously identified as blocking, NOT the full docker harness, which carries far more and is only truly verified when CI runs it. Treat the harness as expected-green, not proven-green.

2. NEW WORK: TYPE_DIRECTORIES NEEDS AN EXPLICIT Arc ENTRY. schema.ts:333 maps Story to "stories" and has no Arc key, so a renamed Arc falls through to the slug fallback and `lore new Story` writes to docs/arc/ — measured, that exact path came back from the local build. Not docs/stories/ (what users have today) and not docs/arcs/ (the plural convention every other built-in type follows: epics, specs, runbooks). The fallback is silent and the path is PUBLIC, so the product-surface rule applies: add `Arc: "arcs"` deliberately rather than inherit docs/arc/ by accident. opum-agent accepted this finding and directed it onto this record rather than leaving it in the message thread.

Open question for whoever executes, NOT decided here: whether `lore new Story` should keep writing to docs/stories/ for continuity, or follow the canonical type to docs/arcs/. Making the directory depend on the spelling used is the confusing option; following the canonical type is the consistent one. lore does not move existing files either way, so this only governs NEW documents.

3. DEPENDENCY: LCLI-558. The alias did not actually preserve link behaviour until LCLI-558 landed (#195) — before it, an un-migrated document resolved to Arc and was then rejected by frontmatter validation. Do not start this task against a dev that predates 5d472eee.
